ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a PWM buck chopper DC motor load circuit. On the left side is the DC power supply Us, and above there is a chopper switch; the switch output terminal is connected to the inductor L, then connected in series with the resistor R, and on the right side is the motor M, marked with back electromotive force EM. A freewheeling diode VD is connected between the switch node and the lower loop. The output current is marked as i0, and the output voltage is marked as u0. Reasoning: The problem gives Us=200 V, R=10 Ω, L is very large, EM=50 V, PWM period T=50 μs, conduction time ton=20 μs. Duty cycle D=ton/T=20/50=0.4. The average output voltage of the buck chopper is Uo=DUs=0.4×200=80 V. Since the inductor is very large, the current is continuous, and the steady-state average voltage satisfies Uo=EM+IoR. Therefore Io=(Uo-EM)/R=(80-50)/10=3 A.

method.method_draft: First describe the image as a PWM step-down chopper feeding a DC motor load through L and R, with a freewheel diode. From the text take U_S=200 V, R=10 ohm, E_M=50 V, T=50 microseconds, and t_on=20 microseconds. Compute the duty ratio D=t_on/T=20/50=0.4. Use the buck average relation U_o=D U_S=0.4*200=80 V. Then use the motor-load average voltage balance U_o=E_M+I_o R, so I_o=(80-50)/10=3 A.
